title.purpose: Card titles and section titles (with § mark).

body.purpose: Default prose, finding descriptions, table cells.

label.purpose: Mono small-caps kickers, table headers, metric labels, severity badges.

shadows.name: hairline-edge
shadows.purpose: The only allowed shadow token — a 1px inset edge on selected surfaces. Never used for lift.

shadows.name: double-rule
shadows.purpose: Editorial double-rule break under page headers. Reads as a print letterhead rule, not a shadow.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for color, border-color, and background state changes.

breakpoints.name: sidebar-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: Below this width, the 232px sidebar collapses to a hamburger.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Cinnabar on ivory. The decisive or destructive action — Run Audit, Disconnect Org, Delete.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Transparent with patina-edge border. The neutral action — Cancel, Back, View Details.

components.name: Critical Badge
components.description: Severity pill with color-mix translucent fill — the substrate shows through. Cinnabar variant signals a critical finding.

components.name: Pass Badge
components.description: Quiet verdigris pass signal. No celebration — just the label.

components.name: Card
components.description: Standard surface container. Flat, hairline-bordered, with a tarnished-bronze header that announces the contents in serif.

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Hairline-bordered input on smoked walnut. Focus replaces the border with cinnabar and adds an inset 1px cinnabar ring — no outer glow.

components.name: Section Title

narrative.overview:
OrgScan is a forensic instrument rendered in oxidized metals and aged paper. The surface reads like a chemically-treated etching plate: warm near-black grounds, hairline iron rules, ivory text that suggests vellum more than screen. Color appears only where a chemical reaction would leave a mark — cinnabar where things are broken, verdigris where they have aged well, parchment where the document has been stamped. Nothing glows. Nothing floats. Everything has been touched by time and use.

The system explicitly rejects the entire vocabulary of contemporary SaaS: no gradient hero metrics, no glassmorphism, no neon-on-black, no celebratory empty states, no Salesforce-Lightning blue. It also rejects the opposite cliché — terminal-green hacker chic — because that's a costume, not a tool.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black surfaces, hue-tinted toward bronze, never #000
Geist + Geist Mono pairing, with mono reserved for IDs / numbers / labels
Hairline (1px) rules carry every separation; no shadow on any element
Signal-only color: severity is the only reason a hue appears at saturation
Numbered findings, section marks (§), tabular figures, leading-zero counters
2px radii everywhere; corners are barely rounded, never pillowy

rules.name: The No-Pure-Black Rule
rules.body: #000 and #fff are prohibited. Every neutral carries a measurable warm tint toward the bronze hue.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Cinnabar, verdigris, persimmon, slate-blue, and parchment-gold are reserved. Each carries exactly one meaning across the entire app.

rules.name: The Color-Mix Rule
rules.body: Tinted backgrounds for badges are always color-mix(in srgb, var(--signal) 12-14%, var(--surface)), never opaque pastels. The substrate must show through.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Identity Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is reserved for record IDs, API names, counts, severity badges, labels, kickers, table headers, and the § mark. Never used for body prose.

rules.name: The Tabular-Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that appears in a count, score, percentage, or ID must use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and font-feature-settings: 'zero', 'tnum'.

rules.name: The Section-Mark Rule
rules.body: Section titles lead with a parchment-colored § in mono. The mark is the project's visual signature; it appears nowhere else.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit on the page. They do not float, lift, or hover. Any box-shadow value outside the allowed inset-1px hairline is prohibited.

rules.name: The No-Blur Rule
rules.body: backdrop-filter, filter: blur(), and frosted-glass treatments are forbidden. The interface is etched, not photographed.

dos: Do use cinnabar (#C14A3D) only where something is broken or destructive.
Do prepend the § mark to every section title.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every count, score, percentage, and ID.
Do number findings rows with counter(finding, decimal-leading-zero).
Do convey severity with icon + label + color, in that order of reliability.
Do use 1px hairline rules and tonal lifts for separation.
Do reserve Geist Mono for IDs, numbers, kickers, labels, and the § mark.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion — state-change motion collapses to instant or opacity-only fades.
Do keep buttons and cards at 2px radius.
donts: Don't use #000 or #fff. Every neutral is hue-tinted toward bronze.
Don't introduce gradients, glow, drop-shadows, or backdrop-filter.
Don't ship Salesforce-Lightning blue or any cool-blue accent.
Don't use celebratory empty states or 'great job!' copy.
Don't use side-stripe borders except the active sidebar nav-item edge-stripe.
Don't use glassmorphism, frosted panels, neon-on-black, or any decorative accent that would not survive PDF export.
Don't name severities with emotional language ('urgent', 'attention needed').
Don't use Geist Mono for body prose.
